body: The technically important boundary is IT versus OT. A supplier could eventually present a respectable SCS rating while its production network, PLC interfaces or equipment-maintenance pathways remain outside that direct assurance scope. So buyers should not let one star label collapse two different risk questions into one. The strongest future signal won't be number of ratings alone; it will be whether procurement teams pair SCS with explicit OT controls instead of treating SCS as a universal cyber certificate.

claims.text: Using SCS as a proxy for total factory cyber assurance could leave OT-specific risks insufficiently assessed.
claims.basis: Inference from the article-established fact that SCS directly scopes IT rather than manufacturing OT
